name: Pulmonary Histopathology Grand Challenge
description: The human respiratory system factually plays a vital role in life. The technology that brings modern medical applications to understanding the imaging patterns of the lung parenchyma has been valuable in both correctly diagnosing patients and saving human lives to some extent. The Advantage of these imaging systems that produce accurate results is the non-invasive examination of the lung tissues and formations. With these advancements, lung image classification techniques have been vital in achieving cost-effective and efficient processes for lung disease detection and pre-diagnosis of patients. The primary goal of this research work is to present different methodologies used in advanced medical image analysis and propose an extended and improved methodology for lung image segmentation which will be beneficial for the medical community in achieving a cost-effective and efficient image processing techniques. The study combined different image segmentation and classification methodologies in order to achieve a more improved throughput from the system. The methodologies that are discussed in this paper include Bi-directional ConvLSTM, which is a hybrid Convolution Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network, and the application of Densely Connected Convolutional Network. This study provided a more advanced architecture to theoretically improve lung image segmentation and processing to aid in the interpretation and diagnosis of lung diseases that aims to be a great value in the medical world in general.
evaluation_method: ROC AUC (and related detection metrics such as sensitivity/specificity, F1)
reputation: Organized as a grand challenge, this benchmark has been used by the medical image analysis community to compare lung histopathology methods under standardized conditions.
notes: Medical histopathology benchmark (non-LLM). Uses high-resolution whole-slide images and expert annotations; evaluation can be computationally intensive and susceptible to domain shifts (staining, scanner differences) and potential label variability.
